title: Branch Manager, Life Insurance ... vs Jasbir Kaur W/O Late Shri Surinder Singh on 9 November, 2009

Branch Manager, Life Insurance ... vs Jasbir Kaur W/O Late Shri Surinder Singh on 9 November, 2009

3STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION, PUNJAB,
         S.C.O. NO. 3009-10, SECTOR 22-D, CHANDIGARH.

                         First Appeal No. 552 of 2008

                                        Date of institution : 5.6.2008
                                        Date of decision    : 09.11.2009

   1. Branch Manager, Life Insurance Corporation of India, Railway Road,
      Sangrur.

   2. Branch Manager, Unit-II, Life Insurance Corporation of India, Patiala.

   3. Life Insurance Corporation of India through its Senior Divisional Manager,
      Jeevan Bharti, Sector 17, Chandigarh
      (All through Life Insurance Corporation of India through its Sr. Divisional
      Manager, Jeevan Parkash Building, Sector 17, Chandigarh).
                                                                .......Appellants
                                     Versus

Jasbir Kaur w/o Late Shri Surinder Singh r/o Village Chajli, Tehsil Sunam,
District Sangrur now residing at Village Ber Khurd, Tehsil Payal, District
Ludhiana, Punjab.
                                                         ......Respondent


                           First Appeal against the order dated 2.5.2008 of the
                           District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum,
                           Sangrur.
Before :-
      Hon'ble Mr. Justice S.N. Aggarwal President.
             Lt. Col. Darshan Singh (Retd.), Member.

Shri Piare Lal Garg, Member.

Present :-

For the appellants : Shri Rajneesh Malhotra, Advocate. For the respondent : Shri M.K. Singla, Advocate. JUSTICE S.N. AGGARWAL, PRESIDENT:
Surinder Singh husband of Jasbir Kaur respondent had taken the life insurance policy for an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- from the appellants on 28.3.2002. He had also taken two other policies; one, for Rs.50,000/- and the other for Rs.2,00,000/-. Jasbir Kaur was the nominee in all the three policies. Surinder Singh died on 29.10.2004. The respondent lodged the insurance claim. The claim in respect of insurance policies of Rs.50,000/- (Policy No.160873601) and of Rs.2,00,000/- (Policy No.160976577) was paid to the respondent but the insurance claim of Rs.2,00,000/- against policy No.161850467 was repudiated. Alleging First Appeal No.552 of 2008. 2 deficiency in service on the part of the appellants, the respondent filed the complaint in the learned District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, Sangrur (in short "District Forum") for the payment of insurance claim. Compensation, interest and costs were also prayed.

2. The appellants filed the written reply. It was admitted that Surinder Singh had taken the insurance policy for Rs.2,00,000/- bearing No.161850467 on the basis of the proposal form filled on 24.3.2002 with the commencement date as 28.3.2002. It is also admitted that Surinder Singh died on 29.10.2004.

3. It was further pleaded that Surinder Singh was addicted to alcohol for the last 30 years by which he suffered a liver disease i.e. alcoholic hepatitis ascites with Ocsophagen with septicemia with cardio respiratory arrest. He had suppressed these material facts while filling the proposal form. Therefore repudiation was legal and valid. Hence dismissal of the complaint was prayed.

4. The respondent filed her affidavit Ex.C1. She also proved documents Ex.C2 to Ex.C12. She also filed the affidavit of Hardial Singh as Ex.C13. On the other hand, the appellants proved the documents Ex.R1 to Ex.R6. They also filed the affidavit of Parminder Kwatra, Manager (Legal), Divisional Office as Ex.C7. They also filed an application for summoning Dr. Amit Soni of Dayanand Medical College and Hospital, Ludhiana along with original record as Ex.R8 and produced the judgment of this Commission dated 18.12.2007 passed in First Appeal No.304 of 2003 "Life Insurance Corporation of India v. Smt. Piari Devi and others" as Ex.R9.

5. After considering the pleadings of the parties and the affidavits/documents placed on file by them, the learned District Forum accepted the complaint vide impugned order dated 2.5.2008 with costs of Rs.1,000/- and compensation amount of Rs.3,000/-. The appellants were directed to make the payment of Rs.2,00,000/- as insurance claim with interest at the rate of 9% per annum.

6. Hence the appeal.

First Appeal No.552 of 2008. 3

7. The submission of the learned counsel for the appellants was that Surinder Singh assured had suppressed material facts. Hence it was prayed that the appeal be accepted and the impugned judgment dated 2.5.2008 be set aside.

8. On the other hand, the submission of the learned counsel for the respondent was that there was no merit in the present appeal and the same be dismissed.

9. Record has been perused. Submissions have been considered.

10. Admitted facts are that Surinder Singh husband of Jasbir Kaur respondent had taken the insurance policy for an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- by filling the proposal form on 24.3.2002 and it was made effective from 28.3.2002. Said Surinder Singh had died on 29.10.2004. The insurance claim was lodged by the respondent which was repudiated by the appellants.

11. The appellants have pleaded that Surinder Singh was chronic alcoholic. He had a liver disease prior to the filling of the proposal form and he had suppressed these facts. Therefore the repudiation was legal and valid.

12. So far as the law on the subject is concerned, it is not disputed that the contract of insurance is based on the principle of uberrima fides i.e. of utmost good faith and both the parties are morally bound to disclose the true facts which are in their knowledge. The Hon'ble Supreme Court was pleased to lay down the law in which the Insurance Company has the right to repudiate the insurance claim in the judgment reported as "Mithoolal Nayak v. Life Insurance Corporation of India" AIR 1962 Supreme Court 814. Their Lordships were pleased to hold that the insurance companies are to prove the following three conditions for repudiating the claim:-

"(a) the statement must be on a material matter or must suppress facts which it was material to disclose;
(b) the suppression must be fraudulently made by the policy-holder; and First Appeal No.552 of 2008. 4
(c) the policy-holder must have known at the time of making the statement that it was false or that it suppressed the facts which it was material to disclose."

13. It is also the settled law that the onus is on the Insurance Company to prove these conditions in support of the plea of repudiation.

14. In the present case the proposal form dated 24.3.2002 filled by Surinder Singh has been proved as Ex.R1 according to which he had given the following answers in response to question No.11 as under:-

11 Do you use or have you ever used (i) Alcoholic Drinks? No What has been your usual state of health? Good

15. The appellants have also proved Ex.R3 which is the certificate of hospital treatment in form No.3816 issued by Dr. Monika Arya in Dayanand Medical College and Hospital, Ludhiana where Surinder Singh was admitted on 9.9.2004 and where he died on 29.10.2004. It was reported in answer to Question 11 in this document that Surinder Singh was a chronic alcoholic for the last 30 years.

16. Learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the non-disclosure of the insured being a chronic alcoholic amounted to suppression of material fact. He has placed reliance on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported as "P.C. Chacko and another v. Chairman, Life Insurance Corporation of India and others" 2008(1) RCR (Civil) 126, another judgment of Hon'ble National Commission reported as "Prema & ors. v. Life Insurance Corporation of India Ltd." 2007(1) CPC 58 and the judgment of this Commission dated 18.12.2007 passed in First Appeal No.304 of 2003 "Life Insurance Corporation of India v. Smt. Piari Devi and others".

17. Document Ex.R3 only reveals that Surinder Singh was alcoholic prior to the filling of the proposal form but there is no evidence if he is suffering from any other disease prior to the filling of the proposal form on 24.3.2002. First Appeal No.552 of 2008. 5

18. It has been held by this Commission in First Appeal No.1585 of 2006 titled as "Branch Manager, LIC, Unit No.2, Hall Bazar, Amritsar and another Versus Rahul Sehgal" decided on 20.12.2007 as under : -

"11. The learned counsel for the appellants submit that this medical record has proved that Rohit Sehgal was alcoholic for the last 15 years, and therefore, this habit of the insured led to the disease and had become a cause of his death.
12. This submission has been considered. It is a far fetched argument. Taking liquor is not a material fact. Moreover, taking liquor is not a disease. Almost everybody takes liquor with few exceptions. Again, it varies whether one takes liquor in larger quantity or takes only small dose like medicine; whether one takes regularly or occasionally. This report does not clarify these details. If consumption of liquor was a disease, the insured would not have survived for 15 years. He would have died even prior to filling of revival form. Therefore, taking alcohol was not a material fact the suppression of which can entitle the appellants to repudiate the claim."

15. It cannot be believed if heavy intake of liquor needs 20 years for a person to die. Heavy intake of alcohol could have consumed a person in a short time and if Kulwant Singh had been taking heavy alcohol as opined by Dr. Yash P. Mehra in his report, Ex.R5, he could not have First Appeal No.552 of 2008. 6 survived for 20 years and would have died before filling the proposal form."

19. So far as the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in P.C. Chacko's case is concerned the facts of that case were different. In that case the insured had suppressed the fact of major operation which he undertook four years earlier and the death of the insured had taken place within six months. It was also held on the facts of that case that the insurance policy was obtained by the insured fraudulently. In the present case, as discussed above, the taking of liquor was not a disease. If it had been so Surinder Singh would have died long earlier and would not have survived for 30 years after becoming chronic alcoholic.

20. In Prema's judgment also the facts were different. The insured was hospitalized prior to filling of the proposal form for the problem of diabetes which was caused by alcoholic hepatitis. It means, therefore, that the insured was suffering from serious disease besides being alcoholic. In the present case, there is no evidence if Surinder Singh was suffering from any other disease prior to the filling of proposal form on 24.3.2002. Therefore, Prema's judgment is also not applicable to the facts of the present case. So far as the judgment of this Commission in Piari Devi's case is concerned again the facts were different. In that case the insured was also suffering from Myocardial Infarction which was kept concealed. Therefore the facts in Piari Devi's case were also different.

21. As discussed above, it is only the concealment or suppression of material facts which can entitle the Insurance Company to repudiate the claim. In the present case it is only proved that Surinder Singh was an alcoholic which is neither disease nor authorizes the appellants to repudiate the insurance claim.

22. It was further submitted by the learned counsel for the appellants that the rate of interest awarded is excessive. Reference was made to the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court reported as "Dharampal & others v. U.P. State Road Transport Corporation", AIR 2008 S.C. 2312.

First Appeal No.552 of 2008. 7

23. We find merit in this submission. The rate of interest awarded by the learned District Forum @ 9% per annum is excessive. It was held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Dharampal's case that the prevailing Bank rate of interest was 7.5% and the rate of interest should be awarded at the bank rate.

24. Therefore the rate of interest is reduced from 9% p.a. to 7.5% p.a.

25. Accordingly this appeal is partly accepted and the impugned order dated 2.5.2008 is modified to that extent.

26. The appellants had deposited an amount of Rs.25,000/- with this Commission at the time of filing of the appeal i.e. on 5.6.2008. In pursuance of the order dated 4.7.2008, the appellants also deposited an amount of Rs.2,47,308/- with this Commission on 11.9.2008. These amounts of Rs.25,000/- and Rs.2,47,308/- with interest accrued thereon, if any, be remitted by the registry to the respondent by way of a crossed cheque/demand draft after the expiry of 45 days under intimation to the learned District Forum and to the appellants.

27. Remaining amount, if any, shall be paid by the appellants to the respondent.

28. The arguments were heard in this case on 27.10.2009 and the order was reserved. Now, the order be communicated to the parties.

29. The appeal could not be decided within the statutory period due to heavy pendency of court cases.


                                                  (JUSTICE S.N. AGGARWAL)
                                                        PRESIDENT



                                         (LT. COL. DARSHAN SINGH [RETD.])
